lots.what_it_is: Mahogany mercury stick barometer with broken swan-neck pediment, glazed door over an engraved brass register plate reading BAROMETER at the top, weather words (Very Dry, Set Fair, Fair, Change, Rain, Much Rain, Stormy) and 28 to 31 inch scale with vernier, no thermometer. Signed lower left and right 'A. R... Fecit'; the surname is not legible even when enlarged. Georgian or early Victorian type, sold as not working.

asking.note: Page opened (condition report PDF). George III mahogany stick barometer signed A.P. Tarone & Co London, silvered vernier dial, alcohol thermometer, break-arch pediment, 96 cm. The report says it has a gap in the mercury and does not appear to be working, with a cracked and repaired cistern cover, so it is very close to our lot's condition. Estimate only, so ASKING. A$152 to A$228 at 1 GBP = 1.8984 AUD (open.er-api.com, 14 Oct 2026); midpoint A$190.

asking.venue: Kembery Antique Clocks via Antiques Atlas (UK)
asking.note: Page opened. London stick barometer by Canti, dealer stock and presumably restored and working. 'Sold' on a dealer page shows the listed asking price, not a confirmed price paid. Same page also has Galli Edinburgh GBP 1,650 (A$3,132) and a fine George III London example GBP 3,395. This is the restored-retail ceiling, well above a non-working auction piece. Rate 1.8984.

lots.guide_summary: Range rests on one close ASKING entry only (Toovey's estimate GBP 80-120, A$152-228, for a non-working George III stick barometer): 0 sold, 0 unsold, 1 asking. Restored UK dealer pieces are asked at GBP 750 and up (A$1,424+), which is a retail ceiling and not part of the range. Rate 1 GBP = 1.8984 AUD.
lots.working: No verified SOLD entry outside Gowans of a comparable barometer in the last 24 months, so both maximums are 0. (Woolley and Wallis GBP 227 could not be opened; Harper Field GBP 2,800 is a named maker with no date on the page.)
lots.confidence_reason: Maker's surname not readable, and outside Gowans the only comparable evidence is one auction estimate. No opened SOLD entry.
lots.dropped_entries: Woolley and Wallis GBP 227 (3 Oct 2024): page returned empty, snippet only, and over 24 months old, dropped. Harper Field GBP 2,800 Ramsden: page opened, but no date on the page and a notable named maker in better condition, not comparable, dropped. Waddingtons CAD 984 (2016): page opened, but 10 years old and an inlaid Hilliard with a hygrometer, a different and better piece, dropped. 1stDibs T. Taylor USD 7,495: page opened but shows no price, and it is a fully restored US retail piece, dropped. Carters 980591: HTTP 429, no price seen, dropped.
lots.key_photo_findings: Enlarged plate: 'BAROMETER' engraved in an arc at the top with floral engraving, weather words down the left side, inch numbers 28 to 31 down the right side, vernier slide, signature lower left 'A. R[illegible]' and 'Fecit' lower right. Mercury tube visible. Broken swan-neck pediment with a chipped right-hand moulding, glazed door with side hinge, plain mahogany trunk, rounded cistern cover at the base. No thermometer.
lots.condition: Described as not working. Case shows wear and a chip to the pediment moulding; plate dirty but legible; glass intact in the photo.
lots.question_for_gowans: Can you read the maker's name on the lower left of the plate? Is the mercury still in the tube and is it unbroken? Is the cistern cover original, and are there any repairs or replaced parts to the case or pediment?

lots.working: Keep: lowest same-item SOLD in the last 24 months is A$363 (US$253.29, 24 May 2026). A$363 / 1.198 = A$303, rounded down to $300. Flip: likely resale A$363 (low end, untested risk). Less eBay AU fees of about 13.4% (A$49) and outbound postage of about A$35 for a heavy console = A$279. A$279 / 2.396 = A$116, rounded down to $115. Caveat: all comps were tested working and ours is untested, so stay at or below these figures, and lower them if Gowans says it does not power on.
